                           PETITION FOR REVIEW

      Pursuant to section 19(b) of the Natural Gas Act, 15 U.S.C. § 717r(b), and

Rule 15(a) of the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure and the Circuit Rules of the

United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit,

Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company, LLC ("Transco") petitions this Court

for review of the following orders of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

("Commission"), copies of which are attached:

            Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Co., LLC, Order Issuing
            Certificate and Approving Abandonment, Docket No. CP25-10-
            000, 194 FERC ¶ 61,078 (Jan. 29, 2026) ("Certificate Order");
            Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Co., LLC, Notice of Denial of
            Rehearing By Operation of Law and Providing For Further
            Consideration, Docket No. CP25-10-001, 195 FERC ¶ 62,007
            (Apr. 2, 2026) ("Denial Notice").

      This petition seeks review of Commission orders under the Natural Gas Act

granting Transco'a certificate of public convenience and necessity for its Southeast
 Supply Enhancement Project, an expansion of Transco's system that includes

facilities in Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.        Transco

welcomes the Commission's decision to authorize the project.          However, the

Certificate Order also erroneously granted "a predetermination to roll the costs of

[the project] into its system rates in a future NGA section 4 rate case, absent a

significant change in circumstances." Certificate Order at ordering para. (H).

Under Commission policy, the predetermination of rolled-in ratemaking is not

available if the expansion project results in "existing customers subsidizing the

expansion." Id. at P 45. To avoid such a subsidy, the Commission compares

estimated first year reservation and commodity revenues from the expansion to the

estimated first year cost-of-service. Id. at P 46. The Certificate Order performs

this calculation incorrectly, and, as a result, the grant of the predetermination of

roll-in is erroneous.

      Transco sought rehearing of the Certificate Order on February 27, 2026.

The Commission issued the Denial Notice on April 2, 2026. Transco is aggrieved

by the Commission's erroneous grant of the predetermination of roll-in and its

failure to correct it on rehearing. Accordingly, Transco seeks review by this Court.

      The order challenged here resulted from the same agency proceeding as the

order and notice under review in No. 26-1100.

        19. Under this policy, the threshold requirement for applicants proposing new projects

        balancing the evidence of public benefits to be achieved against the residual adverse

        environmental analysis, where other interests are considered.
